page: Microsoft Azure F32alds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at up to 4.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs, utilizing a single thread per core to eliminate resource contention common to simultaneous multithreading environments. Total system memory measures 64 GB, resulting in a compute-oriented ratio of 2 GB per core. The CPU provides 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, complemented by support for advanced vector and cryptographic instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, AES, and SHA-NI. Local storage includes an integrated 3,780 GB NVMe solid-state drive, while graphics processing units are not included.

Synthetic benchmarks show strong computational capability across single-core and multi-core operations. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU throughput ranks in the top decile at 3,777.06, supported by high clock rates and AVX-512 acceleration, while multi-core stress testing registers in the top quartile at 118,370.62. Single-threaded data compression also achieves top-tier results, reaching 41.23 GB/s in gzip and 18.06 GB/s in bzip3 decompression, scaling to 466.38 GB/s across multiple threads. Memory benchmarks and database operations similarly place in upper percentiles, with PassMark database operations scoring in the top tier at 36,918.93 and Redis achieving 90.37 million SET operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F32alds_v7 concentrates expenditure on high-frequency CPU cores and local NVMe throughput rather than large memory arrays. This configuration optimizes resource density for tasks where memory footprints stay below 64 GB. The primary architectural tradeoff is the constrained memory ratio of 2 GB per core, which restricts viability for large in-memory data structures or enterprise databases requiring massive RAM caches. However, the presence of 3,780 GB of local NVMe storage mitigates high-frequency I/O latency for applications requiring rapid temporary storage or high read/write IOPS without incurring the overhead of attached network volumes.

Workload compatibility aligns directly with compute-heavy, IO-intensive processing. The instance is well matched for continuous integration and compilation pipelines, static web serving clusters, batch processing, video transcoding, and scientific simulation models that rely on AVX-512 vector pipelines. Additionally, database workloads and caching layers that can operate within a 64 GB RAM envelope gain substantial advantage from the high-throughput local NVMe storage array.
description: Microsoft Azure F32alds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz. The instance delivers 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading, paired with 64 GB of system memory, establishing a 2 GB per core ratio. Acceleration features include AVX-512 vector extensions and cryptographic instruction sets like AES and SHA-NI. The instance integrates 3,780 GB of direct-attached NVMe solid-state storage, eliminating network storage latency for scratch space, caching, and local filesystems, while operating without discrete graphics processing hardware. Benchmark evaluations confirm top-tier single-core execution alongside strong multi-core throughput, compression capacity, and database transaction rates. The low memory-to-core allocation provides an efficient compute footprint for applications where CPU cycles take precedence over memory scale. It serves compute-bound workloads, batch processing, static web delivery, continuous integration pipelines, and local NVMe-dependent database engines.
